title: Harborfield SE action log — PoC daybook
content:
Purpose: personal daily scratchpad for Harborfield (retail) PoC. Fast notes, config reminders, action items for on-call window and next steps. Not polished. Use to populate a formal runbook later.

2025-11-04 (kickoff)
- Quick recap: initial network access granted (Harborfield VPC; peering in place). Got customer to share subnet IDs and KMS key alias.
- TODO: verify cross-account role ARN and whitelist our control-plane IPs.
- Notes: customer prefers Dedicated private controller (VPC mode) over hosted for compliance.

Immediate checklist (first 48h)
[ ] Validate KMS key policy with security
[ ] Confirm Egress rules for telemetry: allow 52.23.14.0/24 to 443 (control-plane)
[ ] Upload certs to S3 bucket hf-secrets (ask infra for write access)
[ ] Generate minimal config for canary model routing

Customer-specific config snippets (notes to self)
- VPC: us-east-2, subnets: subnet-0a1b2c3d (private-1), subnet-0d3c2b1a (private-2)
- Allowed CIDR for management (from customer): 10.120.0.0/20
- KMS alias: alias/hf-prod-llm
- Storage: s3://harborfield-hf-artifacts (encrypted)

Initial infra sizing recommendation (rough)
- PoC 2-node pool: 1x H100-80GB (inference node, primary), 1x A100-40GB (fallback, quantized)
- Estimate: 200 concurrency steady -> target batching 8 token latency SLO 300ms p95 (aim for 200ms)
- Keep cache warm (prefix cache for product SKU prompts)

Model and runtime notes
- Model: hornet-v2-7b (customer prefers open licensed), quantized variant: hornet-v2-7b-q4f16 for A100 fallback
- Routing policy: prefer H100 hornet-v2-7b-accel, fallback to A100-q quant when load > 85% or memory pressure > 75%
- KV cache warm command: curl -X POST https://internal-proxy/cache/warm -d '{\"keys\":[\"sku-prefix-\"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Observability: enable trace_id in payloads for correlation with Harborfield cart service (trace key: hf_cart_xid)

Dev/test commands (for local repro)
- quick local: ./scripts/run_local_inference.sh --model hornet-v2-7b --batch 4 --seq 512
- build and push container: docker build -t redwood/hf-poc:harborfield-20251104 . && docker push redwood/hf-poc:harborfield-20251104
- sample inference curl:
  curl -s -X POST https://internal-hf-api.local/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{\"model\":\"hornet-v2-7b\",\"input\":\"check availability for SKU 42\"}'

Open questions / blockers (triage level)
- Who owns the cross-account role? Need ARN and confirmation that it includes sts:AssumeRole, s3:GetObject, kms:Decrypt. (Pinged Marta 2025-11-05)
- Customer requests no external telemetry to third-party APMs; need to set observability to local-only and forward traces via their datadog collector (private).
- Need legal sign-off on data-retention (24h logs) for PoC.

Canary rollout plan (quick sketch)
- Step 0: Deploy controller + two inference nodes in private subnets; smoke test with admin token
- Step 1 (50 users): route 5% traffic to canary model (hornet-v2-7b-canary) for 4 hours, evaluate errors/latency
- Step 2 if stable: 25% for 24 hours with automated rollback if p95 latency > 400ms or error_rate > 2%
- Fallback policy: if node pressure > 80% for >2m, switch 20% traffic to A100 fallback pool

Notes from 2025-11-06 pairing with customer network team
- They require our ssh bastion to rotate keys weekly; ask infra for ephemeral key flow (put into next sprint)
- Provided firewall rule: allow outbound TCP 443 to management endpoint 34.210.47.92 (control-plane). Confirmed via packet capture.

Small UX/SDK issues to surface to dev exp team
- Need clearer error codes when model variant missing KV cache hint (customer saw 503 vs structured error)
- Add telemetry flag in SDK to include hf_cart_xid automatically when cart header present

Quick wins (deliverables this week)
- PR: add canary config template for customer (hf-canary-template.json) -> target: 2025-11-07 (Devon)
- Runbook: one-pager with rollback thresholds -> target: 2025-11-08 (Riley)
- Infra: validate cross-account role and KMS policy -> target: 2025-11-08 (Marta)

Scratch area (phrases to include in the customer runbook)
- "Traffic-first canaries with automated fallback"
- "Quantized fallback to reduce OOM incidents"
- "Token-level billing visibility required by Finance"

Random notes to self
- If latency spike persists after warm caching, add LRU cache for frequent SKU prefixes (TTL 30m)
- Consider enabling batching up to 12 for night windows (low p95 impact expected)

End of page. Will append logs from next pairing session and paste short stack traces when we hit the first memory pressure event.
